bottom_line: In patients with previous myocardial infarction, high-dose atorvastatin vs usual-dose simvastatin did not significantly reduce major coronary events (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.01).
implications: These data support that, versus simvastatin 20 mg/d, atorvastatin 80 mg/d did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in the primary endpoint of major coronary events (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.01; P=.07), while showing statistically significant reductions in nonfatal myocardial infarction (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.71-0.98; P=.02) and major cardiovascular events (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98; P=.02). The results do not support a difference in all-cause mortality (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.85-1.13; P=.81) or noncardiovascular death (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.73-1.15; P=.47) between regimens; they do show more discontinuations for adverse events and more liver enzyme elevations with atorvastatin (eg, ALT >3×ULN 43 [0.97%] vs 5 [0.11%]).

major_points.text: Trial design was prospective, randomized, open-label with blinded end-point evaluation (PROBE) with median follow-up 4.8 years.
major_points.quote: The IDEAL study, a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end-point evaluation trial conducted at 190 ambulatory cardiology care and specialist practices in northern Europe between March 1999 and March 2005 with a median follow-up of 4.8 years

major_points.text: Participants were 8888 patients aged 80 years or younger with a history of acute MI.
major_points.quote: which enrolled 8888 patients aged 80 years or younger with a history of acute MI.

major_points.text: Interventions compared were atorvastatin 80 mg/d vs simvastatin 20 mg/d.
major_points.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to receive a high dose of atorvastatin (80 mg/d; n=4439), or usual-dose simvastatin (20 mg/d; n=4449).

major_points.text: Primary outcome (major coronary event) occurred in 10.4% vs 9.3% and was not statistically significant.
major_points.quote: A major coronary event occurred in 463 simvastatin patients (10.4%) and in 411 atorvastatin patients (9.3%) (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.01; P=.07).

major_points.text: Nonfatal myocardial infarction was significantly lower with atorvastatin.
major_points.quote: Nonfatal acute MI occurred in 321 (7.2%) and 267 (6.0%) in the 2 groups (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.71-0.98; P = .02)

major_points.text: Major cardiovascular events were significantly lower with atorvastatin.
major_points.quote: Major cardiovascular events occurred in 608 and 533 in the 2 groups, respectively (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.77-0.98; P=.02).

major_points.text: All-cause mortality did not differ between groups.
major_points.quote: Death from any cause occurred in 374 (8.4%) in the simvastatin group and 366 (8.2%) in the atorvastatin group (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.85-1.13; P=.81).

major_points.text: Transaminase elevation causing withdrawal was more frequent with atorvastatin; serious myopathy and rhabdomyolysis were rare.
major_points.quote: transaminase elevation resulted in 43 (1.0%) vs 5 (0.1%) withdrawals (P⬍.001). Serious myopathy and rhabdomyolysis were rare in both groups.

criticisms.text: Open-label PROBE design did not have the advantages of a double-blind trial.
criticisms.quote: The IDEAL study was carried out with the PROBE design and, thus, did not have the advantages of a double-blind trial.

criticisms.text: Bias for physician-initiated endpoints (eg, revascularization/unstable angina hospitalization) cannot be excluded due to open-label design.
criticisms.quote: the possibility of bias for some of the physician- initiated end points, such as coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina, cannot be excluded.

criticisms.text: Follow-up duration was shorter than anticipated in the protocol.
criticisms.quote: the follow-up duration was only a median of 4.8 years even though the study protocol anticipated the prespeci- fied number of primary end points to be reached after a median of 5.5 years.

criticisms.text: Primary endpoint did not reach statistical significance, possibly due to smaller-than-projected LDL-C difference and/or adherence differences.
criticisms.quote: One explanation might be insufficient dif- ference in levels of LDL-C between the groups since the observed difference was slightly smaller than projected.

criticisms.text: Higher discontinuations in atorvastatin group may reflect reporting bias given open-label design.
criticisms.quote: This difference may reflect real nontol- erance to a high dose of atorvastatin, but the possibility of reporting bias is pres- ent given the open-label design of the trial.
